common_name: First Light Swamp Sunflower (Compact Early-Blooming Native Fall Perennial)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to moist, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; First Light is a compact, earlier-blooming swamp sunflower selection well suited to a mid-size border position.

directions: Plant in well-drained to moist, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. First Light stays notably more compact than the straight species, generally under four feet, and begins blooming somewhat earlier in the fall season, extending the golden-yellow, daisy-form flower display that swamp sunflower is known for. Its shorter stature makes it more self-supporting than the tall, sometimes floppy species and fits a mid-border position where the species' six-to-ten-foot height would be impractical. Highly attractive to migrating monarch butterflies, native bees, and seed-eating birds during the critical late-season nectar window before frost. Divide every three to four years in spring to prevent center die-out in mature clumps.

common_name: Autumn Gold Swamp Sunflower (Rich Golden-Yellow Compact Native Perennial)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to moist, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Autumn Gold is a compact swamp sunflower selection with rich golden-yellow flowers, more self-supporting than the tall species.

directions: Plant in well-drained to moist, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Autumn Gold produces the deep, rich golden-yellow, daisy-form flowers with dark centers typical of swamp sunflower, blooming heavily from September into November when few other perennials are at peak display, but on a more compact, self-supporting plant than the species, which can reach six to ten feet and flop without staking. Its shorter stature suits a mid-border position and reduces maintenance while retaining the full fall color impact. Highly attractive to migrating monarch butterflies, native bees, and seed-eating birds. Divide every three to four years in spring to prevent center die-out in mature clumps.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; Mardi Gras bears multicolor flowers blending red, orange, and gold tones on each bloom.

directions: Plant in consistently moist to wet, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; sneezeweed thrives in moist soils and is poorly suited to dry conditions. Mardi Gras bears vividly multicolored flowers that blend red, orange, and gold within the same bloom and even shift color as flowers age, a lively departure from the solid golden-yellow of the straight species, held on reflexed-petal daisy flowers with a prominent rounded disk from summer into fall. It is exceptionally attractive to native bumblebees and specialist Helenium-foraging bees during the pollen-rich bloom period. Divide established clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor, and stake in rich, moist soils if plants exceed three feet.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; Salsa is a compact sneezeweed selection with deep, saturated red flowers on a shorter, more self-supporting plant.

directions: Plant in consistently moist to wet, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; sneezeweed thrives in moist soils and is poorly suited to dry conditions. Salsa bears deep, saturated red flowers with reflexed petals fanning back from a prominent rounded disk, on a notably compact, sturdy plant that needs no staking, unlike many taller Helenium selections. Its shorter stature and intense color make it well suited to the middle of a border or a large container, blooming from summer into fall and drawing native bumblebees and specialist Helenium-foraging bees. Divide established clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; Moerheim Beauty is a classic, long-cultivated sneezeweed selection with rich bronze-red flowers.

directions: Plant in consistently moist to wet, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; sneezeweed thrives in moist soils and is poorly suited to dry conditions. Moerheim Beauty, a long-cultivated Dutch selection dating to the early twentieth century, bears rich, coppery bronze-red flowers with reflexed petals fanning back from a prominent brown-yellow disk, blooming from early summer into fall, earlier and longer than many other Helenium cultivars. Its warm, antique color pairs well with ornamental grasses and late-season perennials in a naturalistic border. Divide established clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor, and stake in rich, moist soils if plants exceed three feet.
